title: Surface a compact repository availability assessment
author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4

events.title: Surface a compact repository availability assessment
events.body:
## Outcome

Present one measured availability assessment instead of making users interpret several raw mirror and integrity fields.

## Implementation

- Define a versioned availability response derived from the existing mirror payload.
- Report online versus known nodes, verified cloneable copies, integrity failures, freshest confirmed sync, hosted bytes, artifact coverage, and bounded risk reasons.
- Model `unknown` separately from `failed`; never convert missing telemetry into a healthy claim.
- Use the same state names and risk codes in desktop, browser, and mobile repository views.
- Update the assessment when a source or mirror disconnects, reconnects, falls behind, or repairs its state.

## Acceptance criteria

- The UI makes no claim that is not backed by a response field and timestamp.
- Healthy, degraded, healing, rejected, offline, and unknown states have contract tests.
- Clone is disabled only when no verified route is available.
- Reconnect and integrity repair update the view without an application restart.
- No geographic or network-diversity claim appears because those measurements are not collected.

## Dependencies

None.

## Verification

Run response fixtures through each client renderer and exercise live disconnect, stale mirror, mismatched state, repair, and complete outage cases.

events.body:
## Outcome

Present one evidence-backed repository availability assessment while retaining exact per-object and preservation details.

## Implementation

- Define a versioned assessment derived from known nodes, signed receipts, clone challenges, coverage manifests, route health, and offline recovery state.
- Report online versus known nodes, verified cloneable copies, pinned and trusted counts, freshest confirmation, hosted bytes, branch and tag coverage, large objects, release artifacts, collaboration records, and current offline bundle.
- Model unknown separately from failed and never convert missing telemetry into a healthy claim.
- Use the same state names and risk codes in desktop, browser, mobile, and headless output.
- Link the compact assessment to per-object receipts from #465 and privacy-preserving diversity and coverage evidence from #466.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every claim is backed by a response field, evidence time, and revision identifier.
- Healthy, degraded, healing, rejected, offline, unknown, partial, and stale states have contract tests.
- Clone is disabled only when no verified route is available.
- Disconnect, lag, corruption, repair, repin, route change, and new evidence update without restart.
- Diversity is shown only from the privacy-preserving measurements implemented in #466.

## Dependencies

Consumes #453, #461, #465, #466, and #467; its base response can land before those extensions.

## Verification

Run shared fixtures through every renderer and exercise live disconnect, stale mirror, mismatched revision, partial coverage, receipt quorum, route loss, correlated mirrors, repair, and complete outage.
